area: Part onboarding / back office (catalog + Vendor Setup + bend-order tagging)
summary: Onboarding today is split between two places: the generic Part Catalog CRUD, which lives in the legacy server, and the newer Vendor Setup draft service. A part row is created by POST /api/parts with only part_number, which must be unique (backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:3539-3564; backend/part_catalog.py:346-375). That route is bound with no auth dependency (apps/api/routes/part_catalog.py:10-15, 22-26). CAD upload (POST /api/parts/{id}/cad, operator auth, apps/api/routes/part_catalog.py:16-17) writes the file under an opaque name in uploads/parts_cad and hashes it with sha256. For STEP it runs the native paired-cylinder preprocessor to get bend candidates and a folded preview PLY (backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:3685-3708); STL/PLY/OBJ fall back to the mesh crease extractor (3709-3735). It then CAS-publishes the CAD, the preview and the full bend-spec set in one transaction guarded by a reservation token (backend/part_catalog.py:820-894). The PDF drawing is a separate upload: it is stored and hashed only, never parsed, and is not covered by the reservation (backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:3814-3851). Candidates are reviewed in VendorSetupPage. GET /api/parts/{id}/vendor-setup returns the part_bend_specs rows as immutable 'cad_candidate' marks plus a stale-aware draft (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:205-274). The operator can confirm, remove (with an issue reason), add manual marks or move them, tag the bend ORDER by clicking bends in sequence, group machine moves, and add CAD reference measurements. PUT validates the whole draft (vendor_setup_service.py:89-202) and saves it with optimistic-revision, CAD/drawing-hash and candidate-generation binding (backend/part_catalog.py:938-989). The tagged order is stored only as `sequence` inside the vendor_setup_drafts.draft_json blob (part_catalog.py:284-295). It is a 'draft' with no released/approved state. Its IDs are the uuid4 primary keys of part_bend_specs, which are regenerated on every CAD publish (part_catalog.py:806), so the order is not stable across a CAD re-upload. Nothing downstream reads the draft. The active inspection entry, analyze_from_catalog (apps/api/services/bend_inspection_service.py:593-640), passes only cad_path, scan_path, part.default_tolerance_angle and a hard-coded 0.5 to run_bend_inspection_task. It ignores bend specs, sequence, completed_steps, matching_search and default_tolerance_linear. Nominal flange depth exists only as a transient, CAD-only preview aid computed on each GET (backend/vendor_flange_preview.py:383-384) and is never persisted. Nominal angle carries the explicit caveat BEND_DIRECTION_AND_INCLUDED_ANGLE_UNVERIFIED with units assumed_mm (backend/vendor_native_step_upload_v1.py:80-92). The separate Bend Label Studio (/api/training/bend-labeling, apps/api/routes/bend_labeling.py) is a PLY-only training/benchmark labeling surface with no link to catalog parts or vendor drafts. Maturity: the UI and its concurrency/staleness contracts are well engineered and tested on synthetic data, but this is a demo-grade preparation aid. The output is not a released, versioned 'part recipe' that the engine, the benchmark or a SKU-matched file watcher can consume.

area: Frontend operator UI, 3D viewer and bend reports (Bender's View, ThreeViewer, PDF export)
summary: The React SPA (frontend/react, Vite 8 + React 18 + react-three-fiber 8 / drei 9 / three 0.182, TanStack Query 5) has three surfaces this work can build on. (1) BendInspectionPage (frontend/react/src/features/bend-inspection/pages/BendInspectionPage.tsx, 1888 lines) is the full engineering view at /bend-inspection (App.tsx:81). It polls the job list every 5 s (line 102) and a running job every 2 s (lines 110-113). It embeds a lazy-loaded ThreeViewer (line 42) fed by /api/aligned-scan/{id}.ply, the reference mesh and /api/deviations/{id} (lines 932-944, 1100-1101, 1252-1266). (2) Bender's View is a standalone full-screen route /bender-view/:jobId (App.tsx:65-67, pages/BenderViewPage.tsx) that renders components/BenderView.tsx. It fetches once (refetchInterval false, BenderViewPage.tsx:15) and shows a fixed 'Research evidence only' banner (BenderView.tsx:57-64). It shows backend-rendered static PNG orthographic snapshots, not a live 3D viewer (lines 45-50, 127-171), plus an SVG BendMapDiagram and a 360px per-bend card list with angle and edge-distance (flange) expected vs measured (lines 205-243). Its '3D View' button links to the generic /bend-inspection page and not to the job (line 70). BenderViewPage does not pass focusedBendId/onFocusBend, so bend focus and arrow-key navigation do nothing on the standalone route (BenderViewPage.tsx:59-65 vs BenderView.tsx:30-43). (3) shared/3d/ThreeViewer.tsx (1644 lines) already has OrbitControls orbit/zoom (line 693), fullscreen, zoom/rotate buttons and layer toggles for scan, CAD, heatmap, bend annotations and min/max extremes (lines 219-223, 441-504). All toggles are internal useState, so a parent or kiosk cannot set or persist them. It also has a deviation legend (536-561) and a snapshot capture hook (line 792). The heatmap colours |deviation| from green through yellow to red (deviationToColor, 814-825), but the legend reads -tol/0/+tol, which suggests a signed scale (544-549). BendInspectionPage passes no tolerance, so the scale saturates at the 0.1 mm default (line 197). Deviations come per vertex as a plain JSON float array from the legacy /api/deviations (backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:1458-1478). That will be heavy for dense RoboScan clouds. Honest semantics are enforced on the frontend by decisionContract.ts. It validates a BEND_DECISION_CONTRACT_V1 with production_disposition NOT_AUTHORIZED (lines 38-42), forces every match to status 'NOT_DETECTED' and never colours PASS or FAIL (lines 101-103). It labels bends Observed formed/unformed/unknown (79-86). So no pass/fail verdict exists anywhere in the operator UI today, by design. The PDF is built in the worker. backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:252 calls build_bend_artifact_bundle (backend/bend_report_generator.py:796-843), which writes the overlay manifest, PNG snapshots (including bender_view_*.png, line 489) and an A4 ReportLab PDF (_BendPDF, 522-785). Its URLs are templated with a literal {job_id} that is resolved later by _resolve_bend_artifact_urls (_server_legacy_impl.py:2775-2789). The PDF has a research-only banner, observed formed/unformed/unknown KPIs, 'Disposition: Not authorized', an evidence-limitations box, the legacy estimate, scan quality, the overview image, and a bend table (Bend, Observation, Target/Meas angle, dAngle, dRadius, dCenter, status), followed by issue tiles (_bend_table 735-777). It has no flange-length, edge-distance or line-length columns, no SKU/serial/operator/station header, and no bend-sequence order. The PDF is served via /api/bend-inspection/{id}/pdf (apps/api/routes/bend_inspection.py:28, service 487-491, which only serves a pre-generated file). The apps/api/routes/reports.py /api/download/{id}/pdf route is the general-QC legacy report, not the bend report. Flange (edge-to-edge) distance is produced only in the GLOBAL_DETECTION match path (backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:2405-2407 is the only constructor site setting it). CAD-local/sequence matches will show '-' for the most important metric. Overall the pieces are mature as research and engineering tools: an orbitable viewer with layers, a heatmap, validated bend annotations and a print path. But there is no kiosk or station route, no auto-select-newest, no live push (only polling; an SSE /api/progress/{id}/stream exists only for general QC, jobs.py:17), no controlled layer API, no flange-first table and no production verdict.

Ready file flow: compute sha256 while streaming, then rename atomically into processing/<sha256>.<ext> (same filesystem; otherwise copy+fsync+rename), then register in C1. Files with an unknown SKU, an unparseable name, a non-PLY or invalid PLY header, or zero vertices move to quarantine/<date>/ with a JSON reason file. Duplicates go to archive/duplicates.

area: Benchmark / labeling / truth infrastructure (bend labeling studio, bend-instance labels, CAD reference scoring, corpus evaluator, vendor-setup bend order as future benchmark reference)
summary: The repo has three separate truth systems that do not connect to each other. (1) The Bend Label Studio: humans draw bend lines on raw PLY point clouds. The route is mounted at /api/training/bend-labeling, gated by legacy.require_auth (apps/api/routes/bend_labeling.py:11-15, registered in apps/api/routes/__init__.py:13,35). There is also a standalone server, apps/labeling/main.py. Labels are written atomically as schema-v1 JSON under data/bend_corpus/annotations/human_bend_lines_v1 (apps/api/services/bend_labeling_service.py:21; backend/bend_training_labels.py:312-346). Each bend has only bend_id, line_start, line_end, confidence and notes (bend_training_labels.py:262). There is no bend order, no target angle, no flange length and no link to a catalog part or SKU. (2) Per-job bend-instance labels: a reviewer adjudicates pipeline markers as real_bend, not_bend_outline or uncertain, and draws manual two-point bends in reference_mesh_raw coordinates (backend/bend_instance_labels.py:15-17,30-31). These are stored next to each job's output as bend_instance_labels.json (lines 161-196). They are served at /api/bend-inspection/{job_id}/labels (apps/api/routes/bend_inspection.py:26-27 -> backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:3186-3202). Those review decisions are the most direct existing labels for the Jev question "is this candidate a real bend?". (3) The CAD-side benchmark: backend/cad_bend_reference_scoring_v1.py scores CAD bend extraction against frozen references, matching by exact native-face sets (lines 94-102). It states geometric and angle accuracy as "unscored" (line 134). cad_bend_reference_bounds_v1.py gives optimistic bounds when references are partial. Per docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md:3-120, the latest CAD numbers are 120/127 known bends (94.49%) on the approved 20 STEP files, micro-F1 98.43% on the 12 complete references, and 12/12 on one email STEP transfer test. The scan-side Gold11 physical benchmark is null/0 predictions in its latest run (CURRENT_STATUS.md:606-620). The scan regression evaluator (scripts/evaluate_bend_corpus.py with scripts/evaluate_bend_case.py) defines a case as a corpus part folder with metadata.json and labels.template.json. Its truth fields are expected_total_bends plus a per-scan state, completed_bends, completed_bend_ids and all_completed_in_spec (evaluate_bend_corpus.py:95-113,818-835). It scores bend counts only (531-560), not per-bend metrology. Separately, the Vendor Setup back-office flow (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:23-74, persisted in backend/part_catalog.py:938-989) already captures the core onboarding truth: stable bend feature IDs from CAD candidates or manual marks, an operator-confirmed sequence, target angle and radius per bend, a bound drawing hash, and operator CAD distances with optional target_mm. Saved drafts are checked for staleness against CAD, drawing, revision and candidate generation (part_catalog.py:929-935). However, no runtime or benchmark code reads that draft. Outside vendor_setup_service and the catalog there are no references to it, and analyze_from_catalog passes only the CAD path and default_tolerance_angle into the pipeline (_server_legacy_impl.py:3344-3410). So "CAD + drawing + tagged order => reference => benchmark case" exists as stored data but is not wired into anything. The runtime per-bend record already has the fields a per-bend evaluator needs: angle and radius deviation, expected and measured edge distance (the closest proxy for flange length), line length and line center deviation, and observability and completion states (backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:205-252). Maturity: the label validators and scorers are careful and tested. The integration between onboarding, references, scan evaluation and Jev data does not exist yet. Some docs are stale: they point at /Users/idant/82Labs/... paths and a March 2026 baseline (docs/BEND_REGRESSION_TESTING.md:28-120).

area: External research: ZEISS robotic 3D scanning cell output, ingest/watcher implications, and shop-floor ICP for press-brake QC (per-bend expected vs actual)
summary: (a) Naming: ZEISS sells no "RoboScan 7000 series". "RoboScan" turns up only as a 2004 academic system from CNR, not a ZEISS/GOM product. The closest real match by name is the ZEISS ATOS ScanBox Series 7, with models 7160 and 7260. These are robot cells with 8-axis kinematics carrying ATOS 5 or ATOS 5X blue-light sensors, built for large parts (6000 x 2500 mm), controlled from the Virtual Measuring Room (VMR) and evaluated in ZEISS INSPECT. Source: zeiss.com/.../atos-scanbox-series-7.html. The other robotic options are ScanBox Series 4 (4105, parts up to 500 mm), Series 5 (5110/5120/5130, ATOS 5 on a FANUC M20iD/25, parts up to 1/2/3 m), Series 6 and Series 8, the ScanCobot (collaborative robot plus ATOS Q), and AIMax cloud, an in-line robot sensor for car-body lines. For press-brake parts in a job shop, a Series 5 (5130 "sheet metal ... up to 3000 mm"), a ScanCobot or a Series 4 is far more likely than a Series 7. The owner must confirm the exact model and the ZEISS INSPECT version with ZEISS or the reseller (Capture 3D in the US). (b) Output: ZEISS INSPECT meshes can be saved as STL, G3D, JT Open, ASCII or PLY (ZEISS mesh-editing page). Point-cloud export is not officially documented; forum users export ASCII PLY as a workaround. Automation runs through the Kiosk Interface, whose config `Kiosk Interface_settings.cfg` has a [General Settings / Data Storage] `SavePath`, plus Python scripting (`gom.script.*`, e.g. `gom.script.report.export_pdf`, and STL export calls that take elements, file and `length_unit` arguments). Forum users say Kiosk has no native post-measure script hook, so automated mesh export usually needs a custom patch or add-on. Our parser must therefore accept both binary and ASCII PLY, and STL too. Coordinate frame: the mesh is normally exported in the INSPECT project's current alignment, which is often already a prealignment or best-fit to CAD when the cell runs an inspection template. It may also be in the raw sensor/table frame. We cannot assume either, so the engine must keep its own CAD registration and record which frame it received. Units are typically mm (the export takes a `length_unit` argument), but our ingest should check them with a bounding-box sanity test against the CAD size. Density: ATOS 5 captures up to 12 M points per scan, and a ScanBox program merges many views. Raw ASCII PLY can reach hundreds of MB to GB; a polygonised, thinned binary mesh is typically tens of MB. That size figure is my estimate, not a sourced spec. I found no documentation on whether exports are written atomically. We should assume progressive writes, often onto an SMB share. The watcher must poll and only accept a file once its size and mtime have held steady over N intervals and it can be opened exclusively. It should also ignore temp/partial extensions and prefer a sidecar `.done` marker or a rename-on-complete convention that we agree with the integrator. For Windows/SMB the watcher must use watchdog's PollingObserver explicitly; native events miss network-share changes. Filenames follow whatever the Kiosk/report `project_name` template produces, so a SKU parser must strip suffixes (serial, timestamp, _1). The template has to be agreed with whoever configures the cell. (c) ICP needs: general tolerances follow ISO 2768-1. Class m allows ±0.1 mm linear for 0.5–3 mm and widens with size; angular tolerance depends on the shorter leg (±1° up to 10 mm, ±0°30' for 10–50, ±0°20' for 50–120, ±0°10' for 120–400). Fabricator practice runs looser: SendCutSend quotes ±1° per bend under 24 in, ±2° above that, and ±0.015 in (0.38 mm) bend-to-edge. DIN 6935 Supplement 2 gives bend-compensation values, not tolerance limits, so it must not be cited as a tolerance source. Flange length has two conventions, flat (bend line to edge) and formed (from the apex / outside mold line), and the report must say which one it uses. Commercial in-machine angle systems (LVD Easy-Form Laser, Trumpf ACB-style laser on the TruBend 5130, Bystronic with Pilz PSENvip, Wenglor MLSL) measure the angle per bend and feed corrections to the CNC. Vendor pages do not document per-bend target-vs-actual screens. ZEISS INSPECT sheet-metal material focuses on trim and full-field deviation; I found no documentation of a built-in per-bend flange/springback report. Our station differentiator is therefore a bend-by-bend table (sequence #, target/actual angle, target/actual flange length with tolerance band, status), using operator language and large type on a 16:9 screen. In-repo context: no file-watcher code exists. The only watchdog hits are in research/f1_ciip_v1, unrelated. The catalog does expose SKU lookup at GET /api/parts/by-number/{part_number} (apps/api/routes/part_catalog.py:26), but it is a thin delegate to legacy (apps/api/services/part_catalog_service.py:18 `get_part_by_number = legacy.get_part_by_number`).

risks_and_traps: Do not build against a nonexistent 'RoboScan 7000'. Treat the cell as generic ZEISS INSPECT mesh export until the model is confirmed
Do not assume the exported mesh is in CAD frame. If INSPECT already best-fit aligned it, re-registering is harmless; if not, skipping registration is catastrophic
Kiosk has no documented post-measure hook (forum 3132), so automatic per-scan PLY export probably needs a ZEISS INSPECT add-on on the scanner PC, which is the customer's or integrator's software

Large ASCII PLY exports (possibly hundreds of MB or more) will dominate parse time and memory. Request binary PLY with a thinned, polygonised mesh, and stream-parse the header to validate the expected length before loading
Native FS events on SMB miss changes; also see watchdog issue #992 (PollingObserver can miss new files after deletions). A simple scandir poll with an own state table is safer
Do not cite DIN 6935 as a tolerance source: its Supplement 2 gives compensation values, not tolerance limits
Do not present ISO 2768 values as the shop's tolerance. They are defaults only when the drawing says 'ISO 2768-m'; the drawing or customer spec wins
Flange length is ambiguous (flat vs. formed, inside vs. outside); a mismatched convention produces systematic ~t+r errors that look like real defects
Filename SKU collisions (one SKU a prefix of another): require exact match first and mark ambiguous cases UNMATCHED

area: Production readiness infrastructure (deployment, supervision, storage, auth, observability, CI) for an on-prem shop-floor QC appliance
summary: The only deployment path that works today is the ShermanChat (manual RAG) surface. The root Dockerfile says it "intentionally ships the chat/RAG surface only" (Dockerfile:1-5), copies only chat modules (Dockerfile:36-46), runs node apps/chatgpt_gateway/server.mjs (Dockerfile:79), and render.yaml deploys that image to Render (render.yaml:1-9). docker-compose.yml's "app"/"app-prod" services build that same chat-only root Dockerfile (docker-compose.yml:14-17,78-81), so compose does not ship the QC engine. The QC-oriented docker/Dockerfile.backend copies only backend/ and run.py (docker/Dockerfile.backend:46-47), but backend/server.py imports apps.api.main (backend/server.py:10), which imports apps/ and domains/. That image would fail at import, and its HEALTHCHECK hits /health (Dockerfile.backend:71-72) while the only health route is /api/health (_server_legacy_impl.py:360-363). The worker image and Helm worker run `celery -A backend.tasks` (Dockerfile.worker:65; k8s/helm/sherman-qc/templates/worker-deployment.yaml:34-41), but backend/tasks does not exist and celery is not installed. Helm probes also point at /health (values.yaml:48,56) and the ServiceMonitor scrapes a /metrics endpoint that no code serves (servicemonitor.yaml:17). The k8s/compose/Celery stack is therefore aspirational scaffolding, not a deployable QC runtime. The real runtime is a single uvicorn process: run.py imports backend.server, which re-exports apps.api.main (run.py:60-82). Every route in apps/api/main.py binds thin shims onto backend/_server_legacy_impl.py (4806 lines) via legacy_context.py:13. Importing it has side effects: it creates uploads/, output/ and data/ under the repo (_server_legacy_impl.py:148-154), opens SQLite data/qc_jobs.db (database.py:28) and data/users.db (auth.py:32), and auto-closes stale jobs (:255-277). Bend jobs run as FastAPI BackgroundTasks that spawn a bend_analysis_worker.py subprocess (_server_legacy_impl.py:892-961). That subprocess has no timeout, no RSS cap and no queue (proc.wait() at :997). Bend job state lives in an in-memory dict (:2772), with only a per-job meta.json fallback on disk (bend_inspection_service.py:68-70), so queued or running jobs are lost on restart. Auth is a homegrown HS256 JWT with PBKDF2 passwords in SQLite (auth.py:80-163). It seeds admin/admin123 when the users table is empty (auth.py:246-256). It uses a random per-process SECRET_KEY unless one is set (auth.py:30), so tokens die on restart and differ across the 4 uvicorn workers in Dockerfile.backend:75. /api/auth/register is open and grants role=operator (_server_legacy_impl.py:601-620), which is the same role require_bend_operator accepts (bend_inspection_service.py:38-49). Many mutating routes have no auth at all: part create, update and delete, bend-spec add, job delete (_server_legacy_impl.py:3540,3596,3613,3878,1577), and live-scan start, which also takes an arbitrary watch_path (:4671-4683). Observability is plain logging.basicConfig(INFO) to stdout (_server_legacy_impl.py:52). There is no file rotation, request ID, metrics or structured logs; infrastructure/telemetry, infrastructure/queue and domains/auth are empty packages. The file watcher (backend/file_watcher.py) needs watchdog, which is not in requirements.txt and not installed in .venv, so the constructor raises ImportError (file_watcher.py:262-265). CI (.github/workflows/qc-quality-gates.yml) runs a blanket `python -m pytest -q`, which conflicts with AGENTS.md's no-blanket-pytest rule. It also runs registry/promotion-gate scripts and frontend lint, build and audit. Python dependencies are unpinned `>=` ranges with no lockfile (requirements.txt). The .venv is CPython 3.11 (uv) with fastapi 0.139, open3d 0.19, numpy 2.4.6, pytest 9.1.1 and reportlab 5.0; pythonocc, watchdog and celery are missing. Promotion policy keeps F1 research-only: production_use_allowed=false (ENTERPRISE_BEND_PROMOTION_GATES.md:5-27). The roadmap's product contract requires execution status to stay separate from inspection validity, observed state and conformance (roadmap.md:237-253), and any appliance must surface this as "operator-assist, not autonomous disposition". Maturity: research-grade engine plus a dev-server web app. For a shop-floor appliance, supervision, durable job queue, auth hardening, data-root separation, engine bundle pinning, health/readiness, log retention, backups and an install path all have to be built new.

area: CAD extraction accuracy and nominal values (onboarding extractor, flange lengths, bend order / machine moves)
summary:
The newest CAD bend extractor is V10 ("boundary chain"), at scripts/extract_step_topology_bend_axes_v10.py:186-306. It wraps V9 (scripts/extract_step_topology_bend_axes_v9.py), which wraps V7's legacy.build_features. The V7 module is built on the V2 native base. V10 adds backend/cad_finite_native_curve_graph_domain_v3.py. It uses only OCP (OCCT 7.9.3.1 python bindings; docs/operations/vendor-unfold-preview-2026-09-29.md:56). It does not use pythonocc or cadquery, and its total runtime is about 1.2 s per CAD (docs/operations/cad-email-transfer-result-2026-10-01.md table, extraction job 1.1995 s).

Measured accuracy is exact native-face detection only. On the approved corpus it found 120 of 127 known bends (94.49%) with 0 unmatched predictions. On the 12 complete-reference CADs it reached 100% precision, 96.91% recall and 98.43% micro F1, with exact bend count on 10 of 12 (docs/operations/cad-bend-native-chain-score-2026-09-30.md:12-20). A single random email STEP transfer case scored 12/0/0 (docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md:3-12). The docs explicitly say that angle, dimensions, units and full bend extent are UNSCORED.

The 7 known misses break down as follows (cad-bend-native-chain-score:127-131):
- 3 broad rolled regions with holes or multiple wires.
- 2 planar-to-rolled returns that fail the two-planar-flange rule.
- 2 case17 refusals with RAIL_CHAIN_JOIN_BACKTRACK, diagnosed as negative join steps of about 2-4e-13 (CURRENT_STATUS.md:47-58).
SLDPRT input is unsupported (STEP only).

The critical integration finding is that V10 is NOT wired into the active path. The live STEP upload goes from apps/api/routes/part_catalog.py:16 into backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:3693-3705, then backend/vendor_native_step_upload_v1.py:406-409, then vendor_unfold_preview._read_native. That function imports the ORIGINAL scripts/extract_step_topology_bend_axes.py (V1; backend/vendor_unfold_preview.py:1129). backend/vendor_flange_preview.py:18 also imports V1. V10 exists only in offline campaign runners such as scripts/evaluate_vendor_cad_corpus_v9.py and scripts/evaluate_cad_email_transfer_v2.py.

V10 output also does not fit the upload adapter. vendor_native_step_upload_v1._axis_rows requires exactly 2 radii, exactly 2 angular_sweeps_deg and surface_count==2 (vendor_native_step_upload_v1.py:113-127). V7/V10 features emit a one-element angular_sweeps_deg list (extract_step_topology_bend_axes_v7.py:300) and can have surface_count>2. Swapping V10 in naively would therefore reject every bend with SPLIT_OR_AMBIGUOUS_BEND_SKINS.

On nominals, V10 gives the following per bend:
- inner/outer radii and thickness as radius_separation (material_thickness_proven=False).
- sweep (turn) angle.
- a canonical bend line at mid-thickness, half-angular turn (v7:292-299). For V10-added features this line is only a "strict interior core", not the full extent (v10 domain_receipt marker_extent_semantics).
It gives NO flange lengths, no up/down direction, no flange identity and no bend-order hints.

Flange lengths exist only in narrow side paths:
- backend/vendor_flange_preview.py:230-288 gives one nominal_flange_depth_mm per bend (tangent edge to the opposite straight outer rail). It covers only the smaller flange of simple web+flange parts, and abstains otherwise.
- backend/cad_guided_native_features.py:214-243 handles only rectangular flanges and is offline-only.
- The runtime scan comparison only computes an edge-to-edge tip distance (backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:369-404, 2340-2361). That is not per-flange length. Its expected value comes from the mesh-derived CAD spec.

The scan inspection path re-extracts CAD bends from a tessellated mesh. backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:161-174 calls bend_inspection_pipeline.py:4012-4025 with use_part_truth_hints=False. It never consumes the catalog bend specs, the vendor-setup marks, the sequence or the machine moves; only vendor_setup_service and part_catalog reference the draft. So the onboarding tags do not reach the engine today.

The mesh detector's angle is the included angle (180 - angle between normals, using abs(cos); bend_detector.py:1767-1771). The native path's target_angle is the sweep (vendor_native_step_upload_v1.py:129-132). These conventions agree only at 90 degrees.

Human correction and bend-order tagging already exist and are mature at the API level. VendorSetupDraft (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:24-74) has:
- marks with source cad_candidate or manual, and issue missing / wrong_location / not_a_bend.
- immutable CAD candidates, so corrections are added rather than edited.
- a sequence, an operator_sequence_confirmed gate, and optional contiguous machine_moves (validation at :89-204).
These are surfaced in frontend/react/src/features/part-catalog/pages/VendorSetupPage.tsx and in the browser PDF (vendorSetupPdf.ts). Three things are missing: manual marks cannot carry flange nominals, target_angle/target_radius are optional on manual marks, and the draft is not frozen into any versioned 'part reference' the engine reads.

The recommendation is to keep V10 as the onboarding candidate generator behind a new supervised adapter. Add a separate per-side flange-nominal module, then publish an immutable PartReference that the inspection run consumes in place of mesh re-extraction. Throughout, treat extractor output as suggestions that the human confirms or corrects.

summary: I read the source only. I did not run anything, and I did not open any physical data. The active runtime path works like this. POST /api/bend-inspection/analyze or /analyze-from-catalog (apps/api/routes/bend_inspection.py:22,37) calls run_bend_inspection_task (apps/api/services/bend_inspection_service.py:306). That task calls the legacy launcher _run_bend_worker_subprocess (backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:892), which starts the CLI worker backend/bend_analysis_worker.py. The launcher sets OMP and other thread caps (lines ~937-946) and then calls proc.wait() with no timeout (line 998). The worker (bend_analysis_worker.py:143) runs three steps. (1) One registration via domains/bend/services/heatmap_evidence_service.build_bend_heatmap_evidence (lines 133-237). This builds a ScanQCEngine, voxel-downsamples at 1.0/1.5/2.0 mm depending on point count (line 163), then calls qc_engine.align (backend/qc_engine.py:1321). The alignment sequence is PCA pre-align, unit-mismatch auto-scale, flip-hypothesis search, point-to-plane Tukey ICP, then a RANSAC 'ISO 5459 3-2-1' datum refinement. If fitness is below 0.55 it hard-fails (line 169). It also writes aligned_scan.ply and per-point deviations for the heatmap. (2) run_progressive_bend_inspection (backend/bend_inspection_pipeline.py:3952) runs in shared-frame mode, which forces strict positional matching (line 3976). It loads the CAD with load_cad_geometry (428): STEP/IGES go through cad_import tessellation, and STL/PLY/OBJ load directly. It extracts CAD bends with the mesh-based extractors: extract_cad_bend_specs_with_strategy (1429) picks between BendDetector on the CAD point cloud and the legacy mesh CADBendExtractor, and renumbers the result to non-persistent IDs CAD_B1..n (_renumber_cad_specs, 985). It detects scan bends and matches them with ProgressiveBendMatcher (backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:2108), whose cost combines angle, radius, line length, area and position. It optionally runs dense local refinement (3248) and merges by rank, then computes scan_quality (coverage/density). (3) It enriches the report, checks heatmap consistency, and finalize_bend_report (domains/bend/application/finalize_bend_report.py) attaches BEND_DECISION_CONTRACT_V1. That contract has the FORMED/UNFORMED/UNKNOWN ternary and a hard-coded production_disposition NOT_AUTHORIZED (line 148, enforced as a Literal in contracts/ui/bend_results.py:114). Finally build_bend_artifact_bundle produces the overlay PNGs and a reportlab PDF (backend/bend_report_generator.py:787-843). Per-bend output today (BendMatch.to_dict, feature_detection/bend_detector.py:202-366): target/measured angle and deviation, target/measured radius, bend-line length and start/end/center deviations, arc length, and expected/measured/deviation of the tip-to-tip 'edge distance'. There is no per-side flange length. The edge distance is filled only on the global-detection match path (bend_detector.py:2341-2361). For CAD_LOCAL_NEIGHBORHOOD placeholder matches, the measured line, radius and edge fields are nulled (to_dict lines 351-366). PASS/WARNING/FAIL (_determine_status, bend_detector.py:2535) uses one global tolerance_angle plus line-position and arc thresholds. Flange length is never part of the verdict, and there are no per-bend tolerances. Bend order, sequence and tagged identities are not inputs anywhere: the function signature (pipeline.py:3952-3966) has no such parameter, and rg finds no bend_order/sequence in the runtime. The worker runs blind (use_part_truth_hints=False, spec hints None; worker lines 161-175), and scan_state stays None/unknown (worker _resolve_scan_state, lines 88-97). Honest semantics are already well defined. runtime_semantics.normalize_observability_state maps anything not explicitly observed to UNKNOWN. finalize_bend_report demotes duplicates, malformed records, partial observation and abstained registration to UNKNOWN with reasons. The text table header says 'RESEARCH ONLY'. The CAD extractor V10 (scripts/extract_step_topology_bend_axes_v10.py:186 extract_step_bend_axes, which builds on v9/v7 and backend/cad_finite_native_curve_graph_domain_v3.py) is NOT used at runtime. It is referenced only by research/scoring scripts. Existing consumers pin older versions: vendor_flange_preview.py:18 uses v1 and vendor_cad_unfold_pipeline_v4.py:16 uses v7. V10 returns native B-rep bend_axes with stable-for-same-bytes IDs ('STEP_BEND_S{solid}_F{face ids}'), radii, line_start/line_end, axial span and angular sweep (v7 lines 293-307). It is detection-only: the 'certified interior core', not the full bend extent, and there are no flange lengths. Separately, an opt-in native CAD-guided measurement kernel exists (pipeline.py:1766-1913, backend/cad_guided_native_features.py, cad_guided_measurement.py, cad_guided_offline.py). It supports only one cylinder with two tangent planar flanges, and its metadata includes finite_flange_lengths_mm (cad_guided_native_features.py:319). It is not wired into apps/ or domains/ (rg finds nothing). Runtime and memory per scan cannot be verified without running it. There are no source-pinned numbers, and the policy limit is below 16 GiB RSS with one heavy job at a time. The only measured figures are for V10 CAD extraction: 30.2 s summed over 20 CADs and 604,000 KiB peak (docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md:66-67). In maturity terms: the engine runs end to end as a research-labelled pipeline with honest-unknown plumbing. It lacks four things the production target needs: bend identity/order binding, per-flange length, per-bend tolerances, and an operator verdict contract. The cleanest headless entry today is the worker CLI (bend_analysis_worker.run_worker with argparse fields job-id, cad-path, scan-path, part-id, part-name, tolerance-angle, tolerance-radius, output-dir). Note that domains/bend/application/analyze_bend_job.py does not do the shared-frame registration or the finalize step.

area: TypeSafe "Jev" data prep: offline bend-candidate "is this a real bend?" decision model (data export, labels, split, dry-run/live-gated harness, evaluation)
summary:
TypeSafe docs (fetched live 2026-10-17 from docs.typesafe.ai, no API calls made) describe Jev as a text-only System One model behind one endpoint, POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, with Bearer auth. The body is {state: string|object|array, model, questions: {id: {type: noul|choice|score, instructions, criteria}}}. Answers come back as noul (a probability; there is no confidence field), choice (choice + probabilities + confidence) or score (score + legend + probabilities + confidence). Jev is never fine-tuned on customer data. The docs say to add domain knowledge through the state and the question rubrics, then combine answers in code or feed them into a downstream classical model (the CatBoost autoresearch cookbook). For Sherman QC, that means 'train/dev' only calibrates thresholds and a combiner. It never trains Jev itself.

In the repo, no TypeSafe or Jev code, dependency or config exists anywhere in source. Only the coincidental base64 hits in two docs/reports HTML files matched. httpx 0.28.1 is in .venv; typesafe-sdk is not installed.

The best candidate-level, identity-free feature source already exists: scripts/build_f1_scan_only_candidate_pool.py (build_case_pool, line 1123). It tags candidates from 10 generators (strict_blind_owned, bend_hypothesis, cylindrical_standard/wide, plane_lattice, scan_mesh_adjacency, etc.; lines 1216-1227). It attaches finite-support features (_attach_finite_scan_support, line 780) and corridor, normal and two-sided dihedral features (_attach_local_bend_support at line 958, _two_sided_transition_features at line 902). It clusters candidates into cross-source line_objects with cluster_mean_/cluster_max_ aggregates (backend/f1_line_object_clustering.py:78-174) and adds case_percentile_* ranks (line 1092). It then fails closed on forbidden keys such as filename, part_id, expected_count, manual_truth, cad_metadata and split_group_id (INFERENCE_FORBIDDEN_KEYS at line 201, enforced at line 1282).

Interpretable evidence scoring exists in backend/f1_bend_evidence_score.py:125. It returns a 0-100 score, not a probability, with explicit uses_part_identifier/uses_expected_count/uses_manual_truth=False. Two learned selectors already run on the same features (scripts/run_shaked_selector_evaluation.py MESH_FEATURE_FIELDS at line 100, extra_trees/logistic), and truth matching is canonical in scripts/evaluate_f1_against_manual_gold.py (Thresholds at line 60: 5 deg / 4 mm / 0.60 / 0.60 span overlap; match_lines at line 138 does Hungarian matching). Human labels exist in two schemas. bend_training_labels.py stores two-point lines in source_ply_raw with review_status complete/no_bends_present and is the one bound to the active route. bend_instance_labels.py stores manual_bends plus marker_reviews with decisions real_bend/not_bend_outline/uncertain in reference_mesh_raw and is used only by the legacy server.

The runtime CAD-guided path has its own per-CAD-bend candidate-or-NULL list (bend_inspection_pipeline.py:3029-3140). It uses a hand-weighted assignment_score and null_score. An already-wired learned head, bend_unary_model.py, scores case payloads in the worker via a mutable output/unary_models/latest.json pointer (structured_count_reporting_service.py:13-44, bend_analysis_worker.py:227). That head uses part_key and expected_total_bends as features and swallows exceptions silently.

Recommended design: a new backend/jev_prep/ package. It exports a per-candidate state JSONL with no coordinates, ids or filenames and with units in the key names, plus a separate label/split sidecar JSONL. A frozen, versioned question set has Noul is_real_bend, Choice candidate_kind and Score evidence_quality. A dry-run-by-default harness writes exact request bodies. A live mode is gated on TYPESAFE_API_KEY plus --live, pins model jev-1.13.0 rather than an alias and caches by request hash. A grouped evaluator compares Jev against f1_bend_evidence_score and the existing logistic selector. Maturity: the feature substrate is mature and custody-aware; Jev integration is zero.

key_files.role: Primary per-candidate feature producer (identity-free). Key spots: build_case_pool:1123; _tag:250 (candidate_id/candidate_source namespacing); _attach_finite_scan_support:780; _two_sided_transition_features:902; _attach_local_bend_support:958 (corridor/normal-moment/two-sided features, defaults at 966-984); _attach_case_relative_features:1092; INFERENCE_FORBIDDEN_KEYS:201 enforced at 1282. The Jev state exporter should read these pool payloads.

cluster_line_candidates:78 collapses duplicate hypotheses into line_objects (LO#). The 24 aggregated feature names are at 116-141, cluster_source_count/cluster_member_count/cluster_sources at 155-166. This is the natural unit for a Noul 'is real bend'.

score_bend_evidence:125, a 0-100 interpretable evidence score (not a probability) with components finite_run/endpoint/two_sided_transition/normal_coherence/source_consensus/scan_distance/stability/topology, plus a review_queue. It is the baseline Jev must beat, and its components feed the state.

Source of the strict_blind_owned and bend_hypothesis candidates. BendHypothesis:227 has angle_deg, radius_mm, cross_width_mm, span_mm, visibility_state, confidence and bend_class. OwnedBendRegion:287 adds support_mass, admissible, admissibility_reasons and debug_confidence. Accepts part_id (374) and serializes it in DecompositionResult (351), so the exporter must never forward the decomposition top level.

Existing learned GBM visibility/state heads with GroupShuffleSplit by part_key (279-280). extract_match_features:96 includes part_key (102), expected_total_bends (133) and reported counts as features, which is identity/count leakage. Do not reuse its feature dict for Jev.

Existing leakage-bounded selector experiments: logistic/extra_trees over MESH_FEATURE_FIELDS at 100-125, with prediction and scoring separated. This is the classical baseline and the split precedent (frozen dev/holdout slice file).

Active human label schema (sherman_qc_human_bend_labels, source_ply_raw). bends[] holds line_start/line_end/confidence certain|uncertain; review_status complete requires lines or no_bends_present (208-300). Bound to the active route /api/training/bend-labeling (apps/api/routes/bend_labeling.py, registered in apps/api/routes/__init__.py).

Its inference_contract asserts no part id, count, truth or CAD (1244-1249), and the forbidden-key guard fails closed (201, 1282).
Cross-source duplicate collapse into line objects with mean/max aggregates is deterministic and order-invariant (backend/f1_line_object_clustering.py:78; tests/test_f1_line_object_clustering.py:37).

Classical selector baselines (logistic regression, extra_trees) already run on the same candidate features with prediction and scoring separated (scripts/run_shaked_selector_evaluation.py:1-15, 100-125).

Human bend-line labels can be authored and persisted through the active API route /api/training/bend-labeling (apps/api/routes/bend_labeling.py:12-40 -> apps/api/services/bend_labeling_service.py -> backend/bend_training_labels.py).

recommended_chunks.title: J5: Offline harness with dry-run default and live mode gated on TYPESAFE_API_KEY plus an explicit flag
acceptance_checks: the default mode is --dry-run: it reads states.jsonl and writes requests/<record_id>.json bodies plus a summary (estimated tokens, est. cost at the documented $0.042/Mtok input) and makes zero network calls (test monkeypatches httpx to raise on any call)

live mode requires both --live and env TYPESAFE_API_KEY, otherwise exit code 2. The key is never logged or written to artifacts. Only split in {dev, calib, eval} records are sent, and eval is sent only with --include-eval

the client uses httpx POST to {TYPESAFE_BASE_URL or https://api.typesafe.ai}/v1/systemone with a 10 s timeout. It retries 429/529 with exponential backoff honouring retry-after, and fails fast on 400/401/413/415/422

responses are cached by sha256(request body) under the out dir. Re-runs are idempotent. Each response row stores the response 'model' field (versioned id) and usage. The model is pinned to jev-1.13.0, and the alias jev-latest is rejected unless --allow-alias is given

parsed outputs go to answers.jsonl rows {record_id, model, is_real_bend_noul, candidate_kind_choice, candidate_kind_probabilities, candidate_kind_confidence, evidence_quality_score, evidence_quality_probabilities, evidence_quality_confidence}
no runtime module imports backend/jev_prep (rg check in the test: bend_inspection_pipeline, bend_analysis_worker and apps/api have zero references)
focused test with a fake transport: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_jev_harness_v1.py -q

recommended_chunks.title: J6: Grouped evaluator and baseline comparison (Jev vs evidence score vs logistic on the same features)
acceptance_checks: joins answers.jsonl and labels.jsonl by record_id, scoring only rows with is_real_bend in {0,1}. Reports per-split and per-group AUC, Brier, log-loss, 10-bin ECE and precision/recall at the frozen threshold, plus worst-group recall

the threshold, abstention band (e.g. 0.35 < noul < 0.65 -> 'review') and any combiner (logistic over Jev noul + the evidence_score components) are fitted on dev/calib only, written to a frozen operating_point.json with a sha256, and then applied unchanged to eval

the baselines are f1_bend_evidence_score total/100 and a logistic regression on the J1 numeric fields, using the identical split. The output marks consumed/retrospective cases as 'exploratory_not_unseen' per roadmap 369-383
candidate-filter utility metric: recall-preserving pruning rate, i.e. the fraction of negatives removed at a threshold whose dev positive-recall is ≥0.99, reported with bootstrap CIs over groups
focused synthetic test: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_jev_evaluate_v1.py -q

recommended_chunks.title: J7 (optional, later): Extend the labeling UI/schema for the Choice taxonomy and negatives on the active route
acceptance_checks: a new schema 'sherman_qc_candidate_kind_labels_v1' in source_ply_raw stores per-line-object reviews {line_object_ref (geometry, not id), kind in bend|flange_edge|cut_edge|hole_wall|emboss|noise|other|uncertain, annotator, revision}. It is validated like bend_training_labels.validate_labels and written atomically
the route is mounted under /api/training/... with Depends(legacy.require_auth). Router registration in apps/api/routes/__init__.py is a one-line edit by this chunk's owner only
synthetic validator tests pass, and no server import happens in the tests

risks_and_traps: Custody: the actual pools (output/research/f1-corpus-evidence-*), gold labels and split slices live under output/ and data/. Building real JSONL needs explicit authorization. All chunk tests must use synthetic in-test fixtures only, and nobody should run build_f1_bend_scorecard.py or the selector evaluation with its default paths, because those defaults point into output/ and data/.

TRAIN18, HOLDOUT10, Gold11 and the Shaked corpus are consumed or retrospective. Any Jev result on them is exploratory, not unseen-family accuracy. EHO4 and any reserved incoming-email parts must stay excluded and unopened. Do not move consumed cases into 'eval' and call it confirmatory.

Leakage: never put part_key, scan_name, filenames, bend_id/candidate_id, expected counts, CAD metadata or split_group_id in the state; bend_unary_model.py:102/133 shows how this already crept into the runtime head. Treat case_percentile_* and candidate_count as allowed but report them in an ablation, since they encode within-case context.

Jev is not fine-tuned. Its probabilities are calibrated in general, not on sheet-metal geometry. Thresholds must come from grouped dev/calib data. A Noul near 0.5 means uncertain and must route to 'review', never to pass or fail (the AGENTS.md honest-semantics rule).

Numeric-table states may suit a text decision model poorly. Run raw vs verbalized variants with separate hashes and expect the classical logistic or extra_trees baseline to be hard to beat. A plausible role for Jev is an extra feature inside the combiner (the AutoResearch cookbook pattern), not a standalone filter.
Duplicates: several line objects or raw candidates can match one gold line. Without the one-best-positive rule, positives get inflated and the metrics turn optimistic.

Coordinate frames: bend_training_labels uses source_ply_raw and bend_instance_labels uses reference_mesh_raw. Mixing them silently would mislabel every candidate. The pool's frame should be verified from source before trusting the join (it samples scan points without transforming them, as far as the source shows).
Uncertain human labels must become null, not negative, and candidates near uncertain gold lines must be excluded too.

External data egress: even scalar geometry summaries of customer parts leave the shop network. Get the owner's sign-off and consider TypeSafe ZDR or an enterprise agreement before any live run. Never send absolute coordinates.
The alias jev-latest moves (it currently points to jev-1.13.0, while jev-preview is 1.14.0). Pin the versioned id and log the response's model field, or calibrated thresholds will drift silently.

Do not wire anything into backend/bend_inspection_pipeline.py, backend/bend_analysis_worker.py or the domains/bend services. The owner said data prep only. The existing unary latest.json pattern (structured_count_reporting_service.py:13-44, with bare except) is an anti-pattern to avoid.

Do not add typesafe-sdk to the app .venv by default, because AGENTS.md says no dependency changes by default. httpx 0.28.1 is already present. If the SDK is wanted, make it an optional import in the harness only.
test_and_fixture_notes: These existing synthetic tests are safe models to copy. tests/test_f1_bend_evidence_score.py builds line-object dicts inline, tests/test_f1_line_object_clustering.py checks determinism and order invariance, and tests/fixtures/f1_structured_union/ holds JSON fixtures (only the directory names were listed, not opened). backend/tests/ also has test_bend_unary_model.py, but backend/tests imports may touch legacy server code, so inspect them before running anything there. All recommended tests are new, pure-Python, under tests/, and import only backend/jev_prep/* plus scripts/evaluate_f1_against_manual_gold.py, which has no side effects on import (just constants and numpy/scipy). Run each one alone, for example: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_jev_candidate_state_v1.py tests/test_jev_request_v1.py tests/test_jev_labels_v1.py tests/test_export_jev_bend_candidates_v1.py tests/test_jev_harness_v1.py tests/test_jev_evaluate_v1.py -q. No blanket pytest, and no importing backend/server.py or apps/api in tests (J7 excepted, and only with route-level unit tests that mock legacy.require_auth). The network-free guarantee is tested by monkeypatching httpx.Client.send/post to raise. A live smoke test runs only manually, with TYPESAFE_API_KEY set and --live on a 3-record synthetic states.jsonl. In this survey no API call was made and the provided key was not used. TypeSafe doc pages were fetched to the scratchpad: api.md, concepts/system-one.md, concepts/state.md, primitives*.md, confidence.md, models.md, sdk/python*.md, sdk constants (TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL, default base https://api.typesafe.ai, default model jev-latest, timeout 10 s), and the composite-scoring, fan-out, confidence-routing, autoresearch and SDE-cascade pages. Request rules to enforce offline: body ≤32 MiB, UTF-8 without BOM, nesting ≤64, finite numbers only, ≤255 Choice options, 2-10 Score levels, 64k per-request and 32k per-question context. Errors are 400/401/413/415/422/429/529, and 429/529 are retried with backoff.
